claims.head: A shadow job for Dach, Nugent-Hopkins and Kapanen
claims.call: The Oilers’ L2 (Dach, Nugent-Hopkins and Kapanen) spends at least 48% of its 5-on-5 time against the Sabres’ first line, against about 40% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending Nugent-Hopkins’s line (Dach, Nugent-Hopkins and Kapanen) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock has been giving this group the hard job of facing the other team’s top line. Tonight the Sabres’ first line is Benson, Kulich and Thompson.

story.head: The Oilers are searching for answers
paras: The Oilers are winless in five (0-4-1), and the Sabres (11-11-4) lost 6-3 to Pittsburgh on Friday. Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Oilers first in the Pacific (third).

The Sabres’ record (.500) is about what their chances are worth. The Oilers’ record (.679) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.548), largely thanks to their finishing. If the Oilers’ record were closer to their chances, like the Sabres’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 89-81, even though they’ve outscored teams 57-55 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 25-15.

The Oilers (3rd) and the Sabres (5th) both get their defensemen shooting. The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd), but don’t block many shots (30th). As for the Oilers, they lean on their stars more than any team in the league (most). They also have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd), and that could do real damage against the Sabres’ penalty kill (23rd). Edmonton has scored 3.75 goals a game, the third most in the league. Both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Tage Thompson (17 G / 14 A / 31 P in 26 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and five goals in six games against Edmonton since 2023-24. Jack Quinn (14 G / 12 A / 26 P in 26 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. Connor McDavid (15 G / 45 A / 60 P in 28 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, and Leon Draisaitl (24 G / 24 A / 48 P in 28 GP) has a team-high 24 goals, the most in the NHL.

Devon Levi (10-4-0 / .889 SV% in 14 GS) will likely start for Edmonton. Buffalo has two options in net: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (8-5-3 / .877 SV% in 15 GS) and Alex Lyon (0-3-1 / .896 SV% in 4 GS). Luukkonen has started five of their last ten games, including the last one on Friday. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.
At home, Mike Babcock likes to send Dach, Nugent-Hopkins and Kapanen out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Benson, Kulich and Thompson.

The Sabres are newly without Zach Benson and Noah Östlund, and have been without Konsta Helenius since Oct 27.
Tage Thompson has scored in three straight games against Edmonton.
Evan Bouchard has twelve goals on chances worth about 5.2 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
